REPORT 
The Report of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, 
Tourism and Culture deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Culture on the 
recommendations/observations as contained in its Three Hundred and Tenth Report on 
„Functioning of Central Libraries in the country ‟ which was presented to both the Houses of 
Parliament on 3rd February, 2022. 
2. The Action Taken Replies were received from the Ministry on 4th May, 23rd June and 
22nd November, 2022 in respect of all the recommendations/observations contained in the 
310th Report. The replies have been categorized as follows:— 
Chapter-I: 
Recommendations/Observations which have been accepted by the Ministry:  
Paragraph Nos.:  13, 17, 37, 42  
Total:  4 
Chapter-II: 
Recommendations/Observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue 
in view of the replies of the Ministry: 
Paragraph Nos.:  14, 21, 23, 33, 40, 44, 46, 47, 48, 52, 53, 54 
Total:   12 
Chapter-III: 
Recommendations/Observations in respect of which replies of the Ministry have 
not been accepted by the Committee: 
Paragraph Nos.:  11, 27, 50, 55, 56  
Total: 5 
Chapter-IV: 
Recommendations/Observations in respect of which the final replies of the 
Ministry are still awaited: 
Paragraph Nos.:   Nil  
Total:   Nil 
  

2 
 
CHAPTER-I 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY 
THE MINISTRY 
 
NATIONAL LIBRARY, KOLKATA 
Recommendation/Observation 
1. The Committee fails to comprehend how the National Library could be expected to 
function to its maximum potential when the top -level post of Director-General of the Library 
has been lying vacant for several years on the run. The Committee recommends that the post 
of the Director -General in the National Library should not be kept vacant for such a lon g 
time and steps be taken to fill it up immediately. The Committee strongly recommends that 
urgent action needs to be taken for filling up the human resource requirements of the 
National Library. 
(Para 13)  
 Reply of Ministry  
1.1 The vacancy has been advertised in Employment News for the week 29 th January - 4th 
February, 2022 for filling up the post of DG, NL. All the necessary actions are being initiated 
in this regard. 
 
CENTRAL SECRETARIAT LIBRARY, DELHI 
Recommendation/Observation 
2. The Committee notes that Central Secretariat Library, a premier library  
situated in the heart of the capital, is a big attraction for politicians, bureaucrats and  
scholars. In view of its locational advantage, the Committee is of the view that CSL  
should undertake the r ole of advising decision makers on matters of library information 
services. The Committee also desires that CSL should play a lead role to coordinate with 
national and international agencies, associations, Non -Governmental 
Organizations (NGOs), publishers and other stakeholders for the development of  
library services in the country and for deriving benefit from huge collections of  
Government reports and gazettes. 
(Para 17)  
Reply of Ministry  
 
2.1 This Ministry vide Letter dated 06.04.2022 has directed CSL to take necessary action 
as recommended by PSC.  
 
 

3 
 
CHALLENGES 
 Legislation 
Recommendation/Observation 
3. The Committee is, therefore, of the opinion that the Ministry should bring  
pressure on state governments to enact library legislation in the states where it has not been 
enacted covering all aspects like structure of buildings, staff requirement,  
preservation of valuable manuscripts etc. for their proper growth. Libraries in  
Southern States may be emulated in this regard. 
(Para 37)  
Reply of Ministry  
3.1 This Ministry vide D.O Letter dated 13.04.2022 and subsequent reminders dated 
04.07.2022 &  31.08.2022 requested all States/UTs Authorities to take necessary steps for 
implementation of the recommendations of the Committee. Response received in this regard 
from 05 States namely Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tripura, Sikkim and Chandigarh may be seen 
at Annexure- C. 
 Financial Resources 
Recommendation/Observation 
4. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the State Governments may be  
guided to frame rules/amendments in the Act in a manner that money collected for the 
purpose is utilized properly and spent only for the libraries. It should not go to other  
State accounts and be used for other purposes. 
(Para 42)  
Reply of Ministry 
4.1 Information on the money collected and expenditure incurred is being obtained from 
State/ UT Authorities. An interim reply with the data received from 9 States has already 
been provided to the DRPSC (Annexure-A). Other States are also being pursued constantly. 
 
 
  

4 
 
CHAPTER-II 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT 
DESIRE TO PURSUE IN VIEW OF THE REPLIES OF THE MINISTRY 
 
NATIONAL LIBRARY, KOLKATA 
Recommendation/Observation 
1. The Committee also recommended that the Executive Head of Library should be an 
eminent Library and information Science professional with strong technical background. 
He/she may be appointed in the grade of Director General at -least for three years for taking 
up the responsibility. 
(Para 14)  
Reply of Ministry 
1.1 Recommendation of the Committee is noted.  
RAJA RAMMOHUN ROY LIBRARY FOUNDATION, KOLKATA (RRRLF) 
(Autonomous Org.) 
Recommendation/Observation 
2. The Committee, therefore, recommends that central government, state  
governments and RRRLF should come forward and take initiative for proper  
development of public library system in India. They should devise a master plan to  
revive India's public libraries to cater to needs of special groups like children,  
differently-abled, elderly people and ethnic minorities and  achieve the goal of  
information for all. 
 
(Para 21)  
 Reply of Ministry  
 
2.1 It is pertinent to mention that Library is a State Subject as per 7th Schedule of the 
Constitution. Therefore, development of public library system comes under the State 
jurisdiction. RRRLF only runs some Matching and Non -Matching schemes to provide 
financial assistance to the Libraries based on the proposals received from the State/ UT 
authorities. However, as recommended by the PSC, RRRLF has been asked to prepare a 
blueprint to take up the matter with State Governments for betterment of the Public Libraries. 
 
 
 

5 
 
DELHI PUBLIC LIBRARY, DELHI (Autonomous Org.) 
Recommendation/Observation 
3. However Committee notes that membership of Delhi Public Library has witnessed 
decrease in recent times, one of the reasons being Covid -19 pandemic. It has come down to 
1.5 lakh membership from what it was prior to corona period i.e. 1.85 lakh. Being a model 
library created in 1951 in Asia with UNESCO’s technical, financial assistance, it sh ould lead 
other libraries in country and extend all possible help in their growth. Delhi Public Library 
should make all out efforts to increase its membership/viewership in the interest of general 
public. 
(Para 23)  
Reply of Ministry  
3.1 Library being a State subject and DPL having jurisdiction within Delhi only, there 
may not be any scope for DPL to reach out to other Libraries in the country.  
 
3.2 The Committee has rightly observed that there has been a perceptible decline in the 
membership of Delhi Public Library (DPL) during last two years. This was mainly due to the 
COVID situation and also absence of reading habit among the society. However, Delhi 
Public Library has been striving to increase its membership by conducting outreach activities, 
approaching schools/ colleges/ RWAs, distributing membership forms and waiving of 
membership fee. Apart from this, the DPL has successfully launched “free membership 
drive” during December, 2021 and this is going on and will be undertaken in the months to 
come. 
 
 
NATIONAL MISSION ON LIBRARIES 
Recommendation/Observation 
4. The Committee is of the view that public libraries have been neglected for a long  
time now and any change would need substantial time and effort from all directions - 
State, community, private sector and non -governmental organisations. The Committee  
recommends that public library system in India should be modified while keeping in  
mind the latest developments in the field of Information and Communication Technology 
(ICT) so as to provide minimum  network based services for the urban and  
rural populace. Libraries should be developed as Community Information Centre  
models and computerization of libraries should be taken up fast to upgrade them. 
(Para 33) 
Reply of Ministry 
4.1 Ministry of Culture has already developed Indian Culture Portal where knowledge 
and cultural resources of various organizations of Ministry of Culture are now available in 
public domain on a single platform. This project is a part of the Prime Minister‟s D igital 

6 
 
India initiative to showcase information about the rich tangible and intangible cultural 
heritage of India both at home and abroad. India is one of the most diverse countries in the 
world. We have a rich cultural heritage but unfortunately we are ju st able to showcase 10 
percent of it to the world. This portal hosts documents, images, audio -video files and other 
data from archives, museums, academies and libraries across the nation. It has a total of about 
2.5 lakh digital artefacts, with metadata. I t also has more than 9 lakh bibliographic entries. 
The content is presented in 19 categories, such as Rare Books, E -Books, Archives, Paintings, 
and Union Catalogues etc.  It also has 9 categories of content, such as Stories, Snippets, 
Historical Cities, and Forts. The portal is currently available in English and Hindi. The portal 
can be accessed through an App called Indian Culture, available on both Android phones and 
iPhone. 
 
CHALLENGES 
 Organizational Structure 
Recommendation/Observation 
5. The Committee feels that there is a need for uniformity in this area. The  
Committee, therefore, recommends that there is an urgent need to set up a Committee to draft 
National Policy on library and information system. A Committee on National policy on 
library and inform ation system was set up on October 7, 1985 under the Chairmanship of 
Prof. D.P. Chattopadhyaya and its Report was submitted on 31 st May, 1986. It is more than 
three decades and the recommendations made then may have outlived its utility. So there is 
an urgent need to look into it. The Committee, therefore, recommends that a Committee for 
drafting a National Policy on Library and Information System may be set up by the Ministry 
of Culture at the earliest. 
(Para 40)  
Reply of Ministry 
5.1 It may be stated that, in the year 1985, a Committee on National Policy on Library 
and Information System (NAPLIS) was formed under the Chairmanship of Prof. D.P. 
Chattopadhyaya. The final report of the Committee was submitted on 30.5.1986. From the 
ToR of  the Committee, it is found that, the document on National Policy on Library and 
Information System was initially prepared by RRRLF and the said Committee, on the basis 
of its own discussion and public reactions, finalized the report.  
 
5.2 The objective o f this policy was to foster, promote and sustain the organizations, 
availability and use of information; to take steps for mobilizing and upgrading the existing 
Library and Information system and services and initiating new programmes relevant to our 
national needs, taking advantage of the latest advances of the technology; and to encourage 
and initiate programmes for the training of library & information personnel. 
 

7 
 
5.3 Apart from the above, in the 1997, an expert group was formed in CSL for 
strengthening of the Library system. Report of this expert committee is enclosed herewith as 
Annexure –B. 
 
5.4 But, it may be kept in mind that all these documents are too old and there have been 
immense technological advancement after that. The objectives of NAPLIS are  fulfilled in 
National Mission on Libraries, especially through NVLI (or ICP), to much extent. However, 
to have uniformity in Library System in PAN India, Central Secretariat Library (CSL) and 
Raja Rammohun Roy Library Foundation (RRRLF) has been directed to frame a blueprint for 
implementation of the said recommendation of Committee and furnish to this Ministry. 
 Financial Resources 
Recommendation/Observation 
6. The Committee, therefore, recommends that a provision should be made for  
collection of library c ess in the legislation itself, otherwise the libraries have to fully  
depend upon State Government grants as finance remains the main hurdle for the  
development of public libraries in India.  
(Para 44)  
 Reply of Ministry 
6.1 As Library is a state subject and public libraries function under the administrative 
control of the respective State/U.T. authorities, such provision may not be imposed by the 
Central Govt. However, all States have been requested to implement the recommendation of 
the PSC . In response to this, replies have been received from Gujarat, Chandigarh, 
Rajashthan, Puducherry, and Karnataka States, which is given as under:-  
Puducherry:- The UT has not enacted the Library Legislation Act and thereby not 
collecting any Library Cess. However, nec essary steps to enact the Act in the UT is 
being initiated.  
Chandigarh:- The Government has no Library Legislation and has no provision for 
collection of library Cess. All the financial needs/ expenditure are met out of 
appropriate provision in various bu dgetary heads provisioned by Director Higher 
Education, Chandigarh Administration.  
Gujarat:- Development of Public Library System is an important and non -negotiable 
objective for the Govt., therefore, adequate funds for the development of libraries in 
the State is being allocated. This year budget provision has been increased from 37.54 
crore to Rs. 43.92 crore.  
Rajasthan:- Rajasthan Government has already had a provision, in which, 2% of the 
total amount of the sales of govt. book is used for development of libraries in the 
State. Thus, the State does not require any separate cess for development of libraries 
in the States. 

8 
 
Goa: - Information regarding Library Cess pertaining to Goa State Central Library is

 School Education 
Recommendation/Observation 
7. As library is a growing organism, not physically but virtually, new roles, 
challenges and opportunities for libraries are coming up now. The Committee  
recommends that facilities may be provided for online/virtual learning for school  
children. The Ministry should come up with guidelines for large scale digitization of  
various books, journals, manuscripts and many other library resources for catching  
attention of children, especially in the light of Corona virus pandemic. A great  
opportunity exists today to increase the reading habit of general public, academicians,  
students, scholars and researchers in different fields by making various knowledge  
resources available through a single platform of virtual library. Technical expertise to  
make reading resources available with Central Libraries should be shared with the  
state libra ries. If need be, Public -Private Partnership (PPP) model for libraries can be  
explored. 
(Para 46)  
8. The Committee also recommends that in order to keep the interest of school  
children growing, textbooks can be uploaded on the internet. Like the e National 
Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) books, State Council of Educational 
Research and Training (SCERT) books may also be made available on the  
internet. Many school going children are not having textbooks or they cannot afford  
textbooks. Further, copyrights of some of expensive books can be bought from the  
authors and digital version of these textbooks can be uploaded and put on dedicated  
sites. Students from all over the country will benefit from it. 
(Para 47) 
9. By making such res ources available to the citizens of this country in different Indian 
languages, the concept of - One Nation – One Comprehensive learning platform may be 

10 
 
realized, and technologically enhance the user's experience in these Libraries, earlier 
understood in common parlance as footfall in libraries. 
(Para 48) 
 
Reply of Ministry  
 
9.1 The National Digital Library of India, a project under Ministry of Education is already 
in existence. This portal  has objective to collect and collate metadata and provide full text 
index from several national and international digital libraries, as well as other relevant 
sources. It is a digital repository containing textbooks, articles, videos, audio books, lectures, 
simulations, fiction and all other kinds of learning media. T his provides free of cost access to 
many books in the Indian languages and English. Text books of NCERT and 20 other school 
boards, question papers, video lectures, materials for exam preparation, solutions to questions 
of JEE Main and JEE Advanced and several other study materials are available in this portal. 
9.2 Hence, separate action from this Ministry may not be required. 
 
 Low Literacy Rate 
Recommendation/Observation 
10. The Committee emphasises that if the goal for National Mission on Libraries  
(NML) is to be achieved, libraries will have to be upgraded at State and UT level by  
strengthening them. Only then, the target of 100% literacy and improvement in  
standard of higher education in the country can be realised. 
(Para 52)  
Reply of Ministry  
10.1 NML also has provision for modernization of one State/UT and one District Library 
for each State. Hence, no comments to offer in this matter. 
 
 E-learning 
Recommendation/Observation 
11. The Committee recommended that the opportunity should be utilized to create a web 
portal for interlinking of National Digital Library of India (NDLI) with international -library 
portals so as to benefit the masses across the whole country. 
(Para 53) 
 
 

11 
 
Reply of Ministry 
11.1 Since National Digital Library of India (NDLI) comes under the purview of the 
Ministry of Education, comments on the recommendation of PSC have been obtained from 
M/o Education which are placed at Annexure- D for forwarding to the Committee.   
 
 Online Membership and Drives to Boost Membership 
Recommendation/Observation 
12. The Committee is of the strong view that to keep up with the times, Central  
Libraries across the country should permit the general public to join/ renew/ cancel the 
membership of the Library via submission of an online form along with the online  
payment of membership fees. The Committee feels that doing so would give a major  
boost to the membership figures of all the Central Libraries. The Committee further  
recommends that the Librarie s may conduct special Membership drives at local schools, 
universities, NGOs etc. in order to get students and researchers to join the library. This 
would permit increased utilization of the resources available at the Central Libraries.  
(Para 54) 
Reply of Ministry 
12.1 Instructions have already been issued in this regard to all 5 libraries under this 
Ministry for implementation of the recommendation of Committee. Information received so 
far  is as under: - 
Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Public Library:- 
KBOPL is in process of developing the system of online payment/ receipt which 
would undermine the membership drive. 19 new members have also been added in 
view of this drive till 07.07.2022. The form has been provided on website. 
Rampur Raza Library:- 
RRL is a special library and houses manuscripts and books most of which are rare in 
nature. Scholars from all over the world come here for research purposes and they are 
facilitated. There is no membership process in the library. In addition, a museum is 
being developed here and approx. 1 lakh people visit the library every year. 
National Library:- 
To fulfill the recommendations of the Committee, following blueprints are adopted:- 
Special membership drive shall be conducted at Kolkata and its suburbs based 
universities like Calcutta Universities, Jadavpur University, Rabindra Bharati 
University, Presidency University, Sanskrit University, MAKAUT etc. A membership 
campaign calendar will be made in this regard. Special membership drive will also be 

12 
 
undertaken in different private universities. Special Membership drive will be 
conducted at all the major Research Institution (Govt/ Autonomous) like, IACS, IICB, 
etc.  
A list of NGOs related to Academic and Research will be prepared and mass mailing 
will be undertaken to encourage membership.  
Membership drive may also be undertaken during the major Book Fairs conducted by 
the different states / parts of India.  
 Local Schools are not considered due to age restrictions as readers below 18 
years are not permitted for membership.

CHAPTER-III 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLIES OF 
THE MINISTRY HAVE NOT BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE COMMITTEE 
 
NATIONAL LIBRARY, KOLKATA 
Recommendation/Observation 
1. The Committee finds that there is no proper preservation of books/manuscripts in the 
National library in printed and digital format. The library is also not receiving copies of 
printed as well as digital publications published in the country. The Committee finds it 
extremely important that the Ministry of Culture and National Library, Kolkata come up with 
a mechanism for collection , preservation of material and digital publications and making 
them accessible not only to general public but also to posterity since the objective of the 
National Library being a permane nt depository of all reading material produced in India 
cannot be achieved. It is understood that a project has been submitted to develop Repository 
of Indian publications ensuring almost 100% of delivery under Delivery of books Act,1954 
amended subsequent ly in 1956 and 2005. The project has been approved by Ministry of 
Culture. The Committee would like to know how the Ministry is ensuring this. 
(Para 11)  
Reply of Ministry  
 
1.1 This Ministry is not aware of any such project. Thus, National Library has been 
requested to furnish the details in this regard.  
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
1.2 The Committee desires to be apprised of the details furnished by the National 
Library with regard to the project to develop Repository of Indian Publications. The 
Committee would also like to know the mechanism presently in place for preservation 
of books/manuscripts in the National Library in both printed and digital formats since 
having a robust mechanism is a prerequisite for meeting the objective of the Nati onal 
Library being a permanent repository of all reading material produced in India. 
 
KHUDA BAKHSH ORIENTAL PUBLIC LIBRARY, PATNA, BIHAR (Autonomous Org.) 
Recommendation/Observation 
2. The Committee noted that there was no regular Director in the library for the period 
2014 to April 2019 and there was also no board in 2018. Board has been reconstituted in the 
year 2020.The Committee is dismayed to note that under the administrative contr ol of 
Ministry of Culture, the said library had been running without a permanent Director for a 
few years which must affect the functioning and decision -making process adversely. The 

14 
 
Committee recommends that Ministry of Culture should shed this apathetic attitude in the 
interest of Libraries and general public. 
(Para 27)  
Reply of Ministry 
2.1 It is not true that this Ministry is having any impassive outlook towards any of its 
Libraries. The vacancy in the post of Director KBOPL remained due to various 
administrative reasons.  
2.2 Presently, there is a regular Director posted in KBOPL. Also Board of KBOPL is in 
function.  
2.3 Besides, as the post of the Director is going to be vacant on 15.4.2022, the Governor 
of Bihar (chairman of board of KBOPL) has been requested to initiate the process to fill the 
posts at the earliest. For the time being, th e tenure of incumbent namely, Dr. Shayesta Bedar, 
Director, KBOPL has been extended for a period of 01 year w.e.f 15.04.2022 with the 
approval of HCM. The matter is under process for taking approval of ACC.  
Further Recommendation/Observation 
2.4 The Committee is not satisfied with the explanation furnished by the Ministry of 
Culture that the post of Director, KBOPL was vacant for several years due to various 
administrative reasons. The Committee strongly recommends that the Ministry may 
seriously look into the various reasons that caused the position to be vacant for such a 
long period and ensure that remedial measures are taken to ensure that no senior posts 
at any of the Central Libraries stays vacant for a considerable period of time. All the 
vacancies may be anticipated in advance and the procedure to fill them may be initiated 
proactively in advance so as to fill the same at the time of creation of such vacancy. 
 
CHALLENGES 
 Low Literacy Rate 
3. The Committee observes that it is really a challenge for public libraries to attend to 
the needs and requirements of every user in the fast developing knowledge society. In this 
regard, the Committee wishes to point out that young people are more tech savvy so they 
would like to use technology oriented services in libraries. 
(Para 50) 
Reply of Ministry 
3.1 No specific recommendation was made in Para 50 of 310 th Report of DRPSC. 
However, the observation of the Committee is noted. 
Further Recommendation/Observation 

15 
 
3.2 The Committee has specifically noted that young people are more tech savvy so 
they would like to use technology oriented services in libraries. The Committee 
recommends that the Ministry explore all the options in this regard, specially the 
technology oriented services used in libraries  abroad and implement the same in 
Central Libraries in the country. 
 
 Infrastructural improvements 
Recommendation/Observation 
4. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may carry out a special exercise  
across all the Central Libraries in the country in order to assess the need for  
infrastructural improvement therein. The Committee feels that having good facilities in  
the form of well -lit comfortable sitting areas, reading rooms, computer facilities with  
good internet connectivity, etc. is a precursor to increase the usage of library resources  
in our country. The Ministry should come up with budgetary requirements for carrying  
out infrastructural improvements at the public libraries and approach the Ministry of  
Finance to grant special one-time grant in order to finance the same.  
(Para 55) 
Reply of Ministry  
4.1 Library is a State Subject. Only 5 Libraries that come under the control of this 
Ministry, are funded by the Central Government. Besides, Raja Rammohun Roy Library 
Foundation (RRRLF) is an autonomous organization funded by the Ministry of Culture, 
Government of India and is responsible for upliftment and betterment of Public Library 
System and Services throughout the country with the active cooperation of the State/ U.T. 
Library Authorities. RRRLF provides financial assistance for development of public libr aries 
through its various Matching and Non -Matching Schemes towards different areas of 
development in public libraries, i.e. modernization, extension of library building, procuring 
furniture etc. This Ministry has written to all the Chief Secretaries / Pri ncipal Secretaries of 
all the State for better participation in these schemes. They have also been requested to take 
up necessary advocacy programmes among the prominent libraries in their respective 
State/U.T. for robust development of public library serv ices. Similar pursuance may be 
continued in future too.  
Further Recommendation/Observation 
4.2 The Committee is aware that Library is a State subject and made the 
recommendation with respect to Central Libraries in the country. The reply furnished 
by the Ministry makes no mention of the assessment of need for infrastructural 
improvement in the Central Libraries across the country. The Committee therefore 
desires to be apprised in this regard. 
 

16 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
5. The Committee also recommends tha t public libraries in India should focus on  
Reader services by making use of vast Information Technology (IT) resources already  
available throughout the country. Libraries can no longer work in isolation either  
geographically or by sector. Their existence is being relatively challenged by new  
services or products like Google, Wiki, Quora, Social Media, E -Resources, etc. Indian  
libraries cannot remain untouched with these phenomena. The Ministry, therefore,  
should endeavor to keep reinventing, reshaping serv ices, redesigning spaces and above  
all, de -learning age old practices before adopting new models of providing information  
services.  
(Para 56) 
Reply of Ministry  
5.1 Since Library is a State subject, this recommendation has been forwarded to all 
State/UT Authorities for necessary compliance.  
5.2 Reply is still awaited from almost all of States/ UTs.  The information received from 
Tripura State in this regard is as under:- 
Initiative has been taken with the adoption of new technology of ICT and also 
reshaping the library services with the focus of library user centric. Two no. of 
libraries under BCSCL has already been upgraded with the ICT enabled facilities. 
Plan for upgradation of all the 26 public libraries is attached at Annexure- E.  
Provisions for reshaping of the library services in the proposed Bill have been noted. 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
5.3 The Committee is of the view that the Central Libraries should act as a 
benchmark for the State Public Libraries . The Central Libraries, therefore, should act 
as pioneers in utilization of IT resources already available throughout the country. 
Development of robust IT infrastructure for better management of the Centra l 
Libraries should be looked into by the Ministry. The infrastructure developed for this 
purpose can then be shared with the State Libraries as well, pushing them towards 
digitization.

REPORT 
The Report of the Department -related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, 
Tourism and Culture deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways 
on the recommendations/observations as contained in its Three Hundred and Twelfth Report on 
„Review of Central Road and Infrastructure Fund (CRIF) Works ‟ which was presented to both the 
Houses of Parliament on 3rd February, 2022. 
2. The Action Taken Replies were received from the Ministry on 17th June, 2022 in respect of all 
the recommendations/observations contained in the 312th Report. The replies have been categorized 
as follows:—

2 
 
CHAPTER-I 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE 
MINISTRY 
 
 
CRIF State Roads 
Recommendation/Observation 
1. The Committee recommends that the Ministry and State Governments should coordinate to 
address the issues being faced regarding the disbursal of CRIF funds to the State. A high -level 
meeting of officials of the Ministry and the State Governments should take place every month to 
resolve issues pertaining to land acquisition, forest clearances, CRIF disbursal, and other 
problems being faced in the development of NHs in the State. The Committee further recommends 
that a comprehensive Master Plan should be formulated for improving road connectivity to 
important tourism places, cultural places, ports etc. across the country and that CRIF fun ds may 
be utilized for implementing the same. The Committee recommends that the criteria for sanction of 
road projects under CRIF may be modified so as to give higher priority for sanctions to roads that 
provide connectivity to places of tourism and cultur al significance and last -mile connectivity to 
ports. 
(Para 25)  
Reply of Ministry 
1.1 Views of the Committee has been duly incorporated in the amendments to the criteria dated 
31.01.2020 issued on 08.04.2022 wherein it has been stipulated to include the Connectivity to 
Pilgrim and Tourist Centres, Air Ports, Important Monuments and Heritage Places. 
 
 
  

3 
 
CHAPTER-II 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT 
DESIRE TO PURSUE IN VIEW OF THE REPLIES OF THE MINISTRY 
 
Central Road and Infrastructure Fund (CRIF) 
Recommendation/Observation 
1. The Committee notes that through the amendment made by Finance Act, 2018, more sectors 
viz., Ports, Shipyards, Inland Waterways, Airports, Railway track and Commercial Infrastructure/ 
Stations, Urban Public Transport, etc., in Transport Sector besides other Sectors (Energy, Water 
and Sanitation, Communication, Social and Commercial Infrastructure), have been included under 
the CRIF. The Committee feels that the budgetary support that CRIF now provides  to all these 
crucial sectors will help in achieving all round growth of the Indian economy. The Committee 
further notes that the distribution under CRIF has been made more transparent as it is to now be 
decided by a Committee headed by Hon‟ble Finance Min ister as per Section 7A of the CRIF Act, 
2000 depending on the priorities of the project. 
(Para 8)  
Reply of Ministry 
1.1 Observations of the Committee are noted. 
 
CRIF State Roads 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
2. The Committee notes that as per the CRIF Act, 2000 and its amendment vide the Finance 
Act, 2019, the  Central Government is no  longer responsible for formulation of rules for State 
roads. The Committee feels that the Ministry should specify the  guidelines and technical 
specifications that must be  followed by States to construct State roads funded by CRIF. The 
Committee recommends that a mechanism should be put in place by the Ministry to carry out 
random checks regarding the quality of such State roads. This would go a long way in improving 
the quality of State roads being constructed by using CRIF. 
(Para 10)  
Reply of Ministry 
2.1 As per Section 10 of the Central Road Fund  (CRF) Act, 2000 the Central Government was 
inter-alia responsible for (i)  sanction of schemes for State roads, (ii) formulation of criteria for  
approval and financing of  specific State road projects (iii) monitoring of State road projects and  
expenditure incurred thereon, etc. However, as  per Central Road and Infrastructure Fund (CRIF) 
Act, 2000 (i.e. CRF Act 2000 amended by the Finance Act 2018 and 2019) the Central Government 
is no more responsible for these functions. The Central Govt. is responsible only  for the 
“formulation of criteria for allocation of funds for development and maintenance of State  road 
projects including the projects of inter-State and economic importance”. 
2.2 Accordingly, the Ministry finalized the criteria for allocation of funds for development and 
maintenance of State Roads under the CRIF Act, 2000 in consultation with the Ministry of Finance 

4 
 
and circulated the same to all State Governments and UTs vide Ministry‟s letter dated 31.01.2020, 
which was further amended vide Ministry‟s letter dated 08.04.2022. 
2.3      As per the applicable CRIF criteria the list of works proposed  to be taken up on State roads 
under CRIF scheme  are forwarded by State Govt./ UT to the Ministry  for finalisation. Ministry 
finalises the list of works  recommended by State Govt./UT and communicates the finalised list of 
works to States/ UTs and the concerned State Govt./ UT has to do the technical approval, financial 
sanction and accord administrative approval of  these projects. The criteria specifies the guidelines 
and technical specifications based on which the works of State  roads under CRIF scheme are to be 
taken up by the States/ UTs on State roads under CRIF scheme. 
 
2.4 As per the CRIF Act, 2000 the Central Govt. has no role in monitoring of State road projects. 
Therefore, the Ministry has no role in checking quality control of the State Road Projects under the 
scheme. Necessary provisions have been made in Para no. 7 of the Criteria circulated on 
31.01.2020 regarding responsibility  of State Governments for quality control of projects. 
 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
3. The Committee notes the State / UT-wise accrual and release made for CRIF State roads 
since 2014-15 and the State / UT -wise allocation and expenditure made for EI&ISC works since 
2014-15 including BOS as on 01.04.2021. The Committee feels that most of the States are making 
efficient use of the CRIF funds. Since the CRIF fund is non -lapsable in nature, the Committee 
recommends that the Ministry must take up the issue of inordinate delays in submitting the 
utilization certificates with the State Government, at the top -most level. The Minist ry must impress 
upon the State Governments that sincere efforts have to be made to ensure that the projects 
sanctioned under CRIF are completed on time and the available funds are timely utilized. 
(Para 17) 
 
Reply of Ministry 
3.1 The Ministry has been taking up the matter from time to time with State Governments/ UTs 
and recently also the Ministry requested all State Governments/UTs vide letter dated 13.05.2022 to 
ensure the projects sanctioned under CRIF Schemes are implemented ti mely, delays are avoided in 
Utilisation of funds under the Scheme and Utilisation Certificates are submitted promptly. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
4. The Committee takes note of the issue highlighted by the Ministry regarding Bank of 
Sanctions already being high and the Ministry not having any funds for further release as the 
unspent balance and current accruals of State Governments have been completely released. 
Considering the backlog of funds to be released under CRIF which has been caused by Bank of  
Sanctions being high, the  Committee recommends that the Ministry may make efforts to keep the 
Bank of Sanctions within the prescribed limits so that the funds for the sanctioned projects can be 
released to the State Governments on time. 
(Para 18)  
 

5 
 
Reply of Ministry 
4.1 The Ministry generally restricts new sanctions within admissible limits as per the provisions 
of Para no. 6 (10) of the criteria circulated on 31.01.2020. However, at times based on the 
priorities of the State Governments/ UTs, the Ministry  considers additional projects under the 
scheme on a case -to-case basis subject to conditions that (i) no additional fund in excess of 
possible accrual/ allocation of fund shall be sought by the State Government/ UT, (ii) the State 
Government/ UT shall ens ure that the progress of work shall not suffer for delay in payment for 
want of additional funds under CRIF, (iii) payment of bills in excess of possible allocation of 
funds, if needed, shall be temporarily arranged by the State Government/ UT. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
  5. The Committee observes a major negative impact that the Coronavirus pandemic has had on 
the number of projects sanctioned under CRIF during 2020-21 and 2021-22. The Committee hopes 
that the subsequent waves, if any, of the pandemic do  not have a significant impact on the road 
projects across the country and that the Ministry would be able to sanction a greater number of 
works under CRIF in the coming years. 
(Para 19)  
Reply of Ministry 
5.1 Views of the Committee have been noted for needful consideration. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
6.  The Committee takes note of the issue highlighted by the representatives of State 
Government of Kerala regarding the criteria for allocation of CRIF funds based on 70% 
weightage to area of the State and 30% weightage to fuel consumption in the State, and 
recommends that the criteria may be reassessed to ensure that there is a logical, equitable 
distribution of CRIF funds and smaller States are not at a disadvantage in terms of the CRIF 
allocation that they receive. The Committee feels that the existing criteria might be resulting into 
very low allocation of CRIF funds to the North -Eastern States since they are smaller in area and 
the traffic plying in those States is also on the lower side. The Committ ee recommends that the 
Ministry may consider making some special changes to the existing criteria to permit higher 
allocation under  CRIF to the North -Eastern States given their sensitive location and difficult 
terrain. 
(Para 24)  
Reply of Ministry 
6.1 The criteria of distribution of funds amongst the States/ UTs has been finalized considering 
the earlier provisions, views of State Governments/ UTs over the years and detailed deliberations. 
Accordingly, it is submitted that the Ministry may continue with the existing provisions. 
 
 
 
 
 

6 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
7. With regard to delays faced by projects under CRIF, the Committee recommends that the 
Ministry should have a system to identify the pending issues with State and Central Governments 
and the same should be followed up with the Chief Secretary of the States. CRIF funds should also 
be recommended for linkage of inner state roads, small towns to nearby NH roads and when 
linkage between two states is being worked out, it should be ensured that both Sta tes cooperate for 
executing the works on time. The Committee further recommends that all concerned 
Ministries/State Departments viz., tourism, culture, airport, shipping, railways, etc. should 
formulate a master plan and plan of action for their respective  sector and convene periodical 
meetings to carry out the same in a time-bound manner. 
(Para 26)  
Reply of Ministry 
7.1 The amendments to the criteria dated 31.01.2020 issued on 08.04.2022 has stipulated that 
the framework of GatiShakti should be the guiding principle for identification, sanction and 
implementation of the Projects to ensure effective convergence to improve connectivity. DPIIT is 
in the process of on -boarding all State Governments/ UTs on the National Master Plan (NMP) 
portal developed by DPIIT through BISAG-N under PM GatiShakti initiative. This would facilitate 
coordinated and synergised planning and implementation of projects by States and various 
Ministries/ Departments dealing with various infrastructure sectors duly factoring in th e 
requirements and expectations of other infrastructure sectors. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
8. The Committee reiterates its recommendation made in para 10 of this Report and states that 
the Ministry should urgently work upon devising a monitoring mechanism to ensure that the roads 
constructed using the CRIF fund are of high quality. 
(Para 29)  
Reply of Ministry 
8.1 As per Section 10 of the Central Road Fund  (CRF) Act, 2000 the Central Government was 
inter-alia responsible for (i)  sanction of schemes for State roads, (ii) formulation of criteria for  
approval and financing of  specific State road projects (iii) monitoring of State road projects and  
expenditure incurred thereon, etc. However, as  per Central Road and Infrastructure Fund (CRIF) 
Act, 2000 (i.e. CRF Act 2000 amended  by the Finance Act 2018 and 2019) the Central Government 
is no more responsible for these functions. The Central Govt. is responsible only  for the 
“formulation of criteria for allocation of funds for development and maintenance of State  road 
projects including the projects of inter-State and economic importance”. 
8.2 Accordingly, the Ministry finalized the criteria for allocation of funds for development and 
maintenance of State Roads under the CRIF Act, 2000 in consultation with the Ministry of Finance 
and circulated the same to all State Governments and UTs vide Ministry‟s letter dated 31.01.2020, 
which was further amended vide Ministry‟s letter dated 08.04.2022. 
8.3 As per the applicable CRIF criteria the list of works proposed to be taken up on State 
roads under CRIF scheme  are forwarded by State Govt./ UT to the Ministry  for finalisation. 

7 
 
Ministry finalises the list of works  recommended by State Govt./UT and communicates the 
finalised list of works to  States/ UTs and the concerned State Govt./ UT has to do the technical  
approval, financial sanction and accord administrative approval of  these projects. The criteria 
specifies the guidelines and technical specifications based on which the works of State roads under 
CRIF scheme are to be taken up by the States/ UTs on State roads under CRIF scheme. 
8.4 As per the CRIF Act, 2000 the Central Govt. has no role in monitoring of State road projects. 
Therefore, the Ministry has no role in checking quality control of the State Road Projects under the 
scheme. Necessary provisions have been made in Para no. 7 of the Criteria circulated on 
31.01.2020 regarding responsibility of State Governments for quality control of projects. 
 
  

8 
 
CHAPTER-III 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLIES OF THE 
MINISTRY HAVE NOT BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE COMMITTEE 
 
 
CRIF State Roads 
Recommendation/Observation 
1. On the issue of Bank of Sanctions (BOS), the Committee reiterates its recommendation made 
in para 376 of its 296 th Report on „Role of Highways in Nation Building‟, which states the 
following:  
“The Committee is of the view that the existing mechanism of bank of sanctions is 
causing a visible lack of clarity between the State Government Departments 
concerned and the Mi nistry of Road Transport & Highways, regarding the amount 
that the State is yet to be awarded. The Committee recommends that the Ministry 
may look into the issue and come up with suitable guidelines to ensure that there is 
no confusion among the State Gove rnment Departments and the Ministry, regarding 
the share of funds to be received by the State, in any particular year, after factoring 
in the Bank of Sanctions.”  
(Para 20)  
Reply of Ministry 
1.1 The Ministry generally restricts new sanctions within admissible limits as per the provisions 
of Para no. 6 (10) of the criteria circulated on 31.01.2020. However, at times based on the 
priorities of the State Governments/ UTs, the Ministry considers additional projects under the 
scheme on a case -to-case basi s subject to conditions that (i) no additional fund in excess of 
possible accrual/ allocation of fund shall be sought by the State Government/ UT, (ii) the State 
Government/ UT shall ensure that the progress of work shall not suffer for delay in payment fo r 
want of additional funds under CRIF, (iii) payment of bills in excess of possible allocation of 
funds, if needed, shall be temporarily arranged by the State Government/ UT. 
Further recommendation/observation 
1.2 The Committee’s recommendation regarding guidelines to ensure clarity among State 
Governments regarding the share of funds to be received by them has not been answered. 
The Committee would like to know if the Ministry has formulated any such guidelines. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
2. The Committee observes that 10% of the allocation made to States under CRIF is to be 
earmarked for road safety works. Keeping in mind that India has the highest number of deaths in 
the world on account of road accidents and the immeasurable impact that the  same has on 
countless families as well as on the overall Indian economy, the Committee feels that the efforts 
being made by the Ministry in this regard would give a big boost if a higher share of CRIF funds 

9 
 
allocated to the State Governments are earmarked  for carrying out road safety works. The 
Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry may consider increasing the percentage of 
funds that are earmarked for road safety works under CRIF, from the existing 10 percent. Further, 
the Ministry may  evolve an effective mechanism to oversee and monitor optimal utilization of the 
funds earmarked for road safety works under CRIF. 
(Para 21) 
Reply of Ministry 
2.1 Provisions have been made in the criteria dated 31.01.2020 for earmarking of 10% of funds 
for Road Safety works. However, many of the works taken up also enhances Road Safety aspects 
and the Ministry is committed to continue the same. 
2.2 Effective from the current financial year 2022 -23, the Ministry has started allocating 
separate funds of about Rs. 1 ,326 crore for State Governments/ UTs for construction of ROBs/ 
RUBs in replacement of existing Railways level crossings and Bridges on State roads under 
“SETU BANDHAN” Programme under CRIF Scheme. This is intended at enhancing Road Safety 
aspects at these vulnerable locations where many accidents takes place. For this, the Ministry has 
also finalised a Tripartite MOU in consultation with M/o Railways and circulated to State 
Governments/ UTs for their consent. The SETU BANDHAN Programme shall include the 
construction of ROBs/ RUBs on State roads under CRIF which are not considered for funding by 
M/o Railways in any of their programmes. 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
2.3 The Committee appreciates the ‘Setu Bandhan’ Programme under which the Ministry 
has started allocating funds to State Governments/UTs for construction of ROBs/ RUBs in 
replacement of existing Railways level crossings and Bridges on State roads, under the CRIF 
scheme. However, given the worrisome number of road accidents and accident -related 
deaths, the Committee  feels that a lot more needs to be done by the Ministry/NHAI/State 
PWDs to improve road safety in the country at an urgent pace and earmarking higher funds 
under CRIF for this purpose should help in the same. The Committee, therefor e, reiterates 
its recommendation that the Ministry should increase the percentage of funds earmarked for 
road safety works under CRIF from the existing 10 percent to a higher figure.  
 
Recommendation/Observation 
3. The Committee further recommends that the  Ministry may review the existing guidelines for 
awarding of tenders for road projects under CRIF or otherwise, since it is often found that the 
projects get awarded at substantially lower bids than the amount projected by the Ministry/NHAI. 
In such cases, the concessionaire is more likely to not actually complete the work at all, or do it 
with sub-par quality. In light of this, the Committee recommends that the Ministry may either come 
out with upper and lower limits for bidding for road projects or establ ish a mechanism to strictly 
monitor the quality and progress of road projects awarded to substantially low bids. In cases 
where poor performance and sub -par quality of road projects is noticed, the contractor must be 
suitably penalized and their past project record must be duly considered before awarding any road 
projects in the future. 
(Para 30)  
 

10 
 
Reply of Ministry 
3.1 As per the CRIF Criteria dated 31.01.2020 Para 6 , the State Governments/ UTs are 
authorized for administrative approval, technical approval  and financial sanction of the CRIF 
works. State Governments/ UTs are only responsible for finalization of the bid documents, 
invitation of tenders, award and management of contracts, including taking up of penal action for 
poor performance and sub -standard quality of the works/ any defaults of contractors. As per the 
CRIF Act, 2000 amended through Finance Act, 2019, the Central Government is no longer 
responsible for monitoring of State road projects under these schemes and expenditure incurred 
thereon. 
  
Further Recommendation/Observation 
3.2 The Committee notes that State Governments/UTs are responsible for finalization of 
the bid documents, invitation of tenders, award and management of contracts etc . However, 
the reply furnished by the Ministry does not make any mention of the action  taken, if any, to 
address the issue of the road projects which are not funded through CRIF, being awarded to 
bids substantially lower than the amount projected by the Min istry/NHAI. The Committee 
recommends that the Ministry may take up the matter of fixing upper and lower limits for 
bidding for road projects and a mechanism to strictly monitor the quality and progress of 
road projects awarded to substantially low bids, with the State Governments/UTs.

REPORT 
The Report of the Department -related Parliamentary Standing Committee on 
Transport, Tourism and Culture deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Culture on 
the recommendations/observations as contained in its Three Hundred Fifteenth Report on  
„Demands for Grants (202 2-23) of Ministry of Culture‟ which was presented to both the 
Houses of Parliament on 14th March, 2022.   
 
2.  The Action Taken Replies were received from the Ministry on 13th June, 202 2 in 
respect of all the observations/ recommen dations contained in the Report. The replies have 
been categorized as follows:-  
 
Chapter-I: 
Recommendations/Observations which have been accepted by the Ministry:  
Paragraph Nos.: 7, 18, 20, 21, 25, 27, 50, 61, 63, 66, 70, 75, 82, 88 
Total: 14 
 
Chapter-II:  
Recommendations/Observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue in 
view of the replies of the Ministry: 
Paragraph Nos.: 11, 12, 16, 22, 28, 33, 45, 52, 53, 55, 60, 69, 74, 76, 78, 80, 84, 86, 
89, 90 
Total: 20 
 
Chapter-III: 
Recommendations/Observations in respect of which replies of the Ministry have not 
been accepted by the Committee: 
Paragraph Nos.: 9, 15, 17, 31, 35, 36, 37, 44, 57, 65, 71 
Total: 11 
 
Chapter-IV:  
Recommendations/Observations in respect of which the final replies of the Ministry 
are still awaited: 
Paragraph Nos.: Nil 
Total: Nil 
 
  

2 
 
CHAPTER-I 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY 
THE MINISTRY 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
1. The Committee is of the view that the Ministry should make concerted efforts to 
achieve the optimum utilization of the allowed expenditure. 
(Para 7) 
Reply of Ministry 
1.1 It has always been the Ministries earnest endeavor to optimally utilize allocated 
budget. Even though the expenditure was comparatively at a slower pace in the first two 
quarters, spending had picked up in the second half of the financial year 2021 -22. An 
expenditure of 95.10% over approved outlay was booked in the preceding financial year. The 
Ministry will continue its efforts to maintain an optimum utilization of the approved budget.   
 
ARCHAEOLOGICAL SURVEY OF INDIA 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
2.  In it s Two Hundred Eighty Ninth (289 th) Report, the Committee recommended that 
ASI  should develop a smart phone application for the benefit of users to know about the 
monuments. The Committee reiterates its recommendations contained in the 289th Report and 
would like to know the status of implementation of the said recommendation. 
(Para 18) 
Reply of Ministry 
2.1 The beta version of the Heritage Atlas mobile application has already been launched 
by ASI for internal circulation and verification. Th e data correction is in advance stage and 
likely to be completed by the end of this year, enabling ASI to go ahead for launch of the 
application to the public. 
 
CENTENARIES AND ANNIVERSARIES, CELEBRATIONS AND SCHEMES 
Recommendation/Observation 
3. The Committee is constrained to note that under Centenaries and Anniversaries 
Celebrations Schemes head, an allocation of Rs. 110 crores has been made in BE 2022 - 23, 
which is less than the allocation made in BE 2021 -22 (Rs. 144.64 crores) and RE 2021 -22 of 
Rs. 135.18 crores. The Committee feels that programmes aimed at generating awareness 
among the masses about events, personalities, etc. play a vital role in educating the large 
populace of our country as well as international people. 
(Para 20) 
 
 

3 
 
Reply of Ministry 
3.1 The Ministry agrees with the Committee's view that the programs planned under 
Centenaries and Anniversaries Celebrations Schemes play a vital role in educating the large 
populace of our country as well as international people on eminent personali ties and events 
of historical importance. The less allocation of budget under the Centenary and Anniversary 
celebration scheme will certainly affect the programmes/activities to be held under various 
approved commemorations including “Azadi Ka Amrit Mahots av”. There are 14 ongoing 
commemorations for the year 2022 -23 besides 630 Programmes/Activities scheduled under 
“Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav” for the year 2022 -23. Hence more funds will be required at RE 
Stage.  
Recommendation/Observation 
4. The Committee finds that with Coronavirus likely to witness an ebb in 2022 -23, more 
and more celebrations of such events need to be organised. The decreased allocation will   
have an adverse impact and will not meet the desired results. The Committee hopes that the 
shortfall in allocation will be met in the RE 2022-23 to make up for any loss on this account. 
(Para 21) 
Reply of Ministry 
4.1 The approved outlay of Rs. 110 crores in BE 2022 -23 is far less than the EFC 
approved figure of Rs 390 crore for the scheme Centenary and Anniversary celebration in FY 
2022-23.  Hence, the shortfall in funds will be communicated with the Ministry of Finance at 
RE 2022 -23 stage to avoid any adverse effect on the programmed celebrations during the 
year. 
 
KALA SANSKRITI VIKAS YOJANA 
Recommendation/Observation 
5. The Committee is pleased to know about the increase in BE 2022-23 to Kala Sanskriti 
Vikas Yojana as compared to BE allocation of 2021 -22 under the head. The increase in 
beneficiaries will help promote various schemes under the  Performing Arts and give a fillip 
to various activities of Arts and Culture in the country. The Committee would, however, like 
to put in a word of caution that both revenue and capital allocation should be utilized 
properly, and targets set should be achieved optimum to the extent possible. 
(Para 25) 
Reply of Ministry 
5.1 The advice of the Committee has been noted for necessary action. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
6. The Committee notes that Kala Sanskriti Vikas Yoja na is one of the most important 
schemes of the Ministry. This needs to be given special impetus in view of the size of the 

4 
 
country and the number of artists in the field of performing arts and reach out to the 
artists/performers in small cities and rural areas. 
(Para 27) 
Reply of Ministry 
6.1 The advice of the Committee has been noted for necessary action.   
 
 
NATIONAL MONUMENTS AUTHORITY 
Recommendation/Observation 
7. The Committee observes that main roadblocks in speedy preparation of HBLs are 
lack of qualified staff in the offices of the Regional Directors of ASI, less number of Heritage 
Bodies for heritage consultation and the quantum of fees payable to these notified bodies for 
heritage consultation. The Committee, therefore, recommends that urgent s teps should be 
taken to remove all the bottlenecks being faced in the preparation of HBLs, such as meeting 
the staff requirements of Regional Director Offices of ASI, enlarging the list of notified 
expert heritage bodies and recruitment of Hindi Translator s, in order to prevent further 
damage to invaluable national heritage due to lack of heritage bye-laws. 
(Para 50) 
Reply of Ministry 
7.1 ln order to remove the roadblocks for speedy preparation of HBLs, the Ministry has 
taken the following steps: 
 
● Additional number of appropriate agencies/ institutions empaneled for 
preparation and vetting of Heritage bye -laws: The Ministry of Culture in exercise 
of the powers vested under Section 20E(1) of Ancient Monuments and 
Archaeological Sites and Remains (AMASR) Act, 1958 (as amended in 2010), has 
notified an additional 30 (thirty) expert heritage bodies vide Gazette of lndia 
notification dated 09.02.2022, for fast tracking the process of framing of heritage bye -
laws.  
● Preparation of Heritage Bye -Laws: lt has been decided that the draft heritage bye -
laws will henceforth be prepared by these notified heritage bodies and the role of 
Regional Directors of ASI will be of vetting such HBLs and then forwarding them to 
the NMA. The Ministry of Culture is in the process of finalizing a standard Request 
for Proposal (RFP) document to be used by the Regional Directors of ASI for 
obtaining proposals from notified expert heritage bodies in their jurisdiction for 
awarding work of preparation of Heritage bye-laws on least cost method. This revised 
strategy is expected to expedite the process of preparation of HBLs. 
● Regional Directors are to be empowered with sufficient Manpower : Since HBLs 
are now to be prepared by the notified heritage bodies, the estimated costs to be 
incurred for hiring of qualified staff (viz Conservation Architects, Surveyors etc.) in 
the offices of the Regional Directors will decrease since their role is now limited to 
supervising and vetting the draft HBLs. Revised staff requirements for the office of 
Regional Directors are being examined by the Ministry of Culture. 

5 
 
● Creation of posts of in -house Hindi Translators in National Monuments 
Authority: A proposal for creation of one post of in -house Hindi Translator in 
National Monuments Authority for streamlining the work relating lo Hindi translation 
of Heritage byelaws for the purpose of laying them in both houses of Parliament, is 
being examined by the Ministry of Culture in accordance with guidelines of 
Department of Expenditure on the subject. Simultaneously, th e proposal for engaging 
2 (two) consultants for handling the work of Hindi translation of Heritage bye -laws, 
as an interim arrangement, is being considered. 
 
SUPPORT TO ACADEMIES, MUSEUMS, LIBRARIES, BUDDHIST TIBETAN 
INSTITUTIONS AND MEMORIALS 
Recommendation/Observation 
8. The Committee hopes and urges the Ministry of Culture to ensure that allocations are 
fully spent and not surrendered at the last moment. 
(Para 61) 
Reply of Ministry 
8.1 The recommendation is fully complied to in FY 2021 -22 and noted for future 
financial years. 
 
ARTISTS PENSION SCHEME AND WELFARE FUND 
Recommendation/Observation 
9. The Committee, therefore, strongly reiterates that the pension amount needs to be 
reviewed without further delay and it should be made respectable for a person w ho has 
contributed to the society and country in continuing the various art forms. 
(Para 63) 
Reply of Ministry 
9.1 The recommendation is noted. The monthly pension has been revised to Rs.6,000/ - 
from Rs.4,000/ - for the Artistes of 60 years of age and above  under the Artist Pension 
Scheme. The order in this regard will be issued soon. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
10. The Committee is not satisfied with the reason advanced by the Ministry and 
recommends that the Ministry should be rather proactive in such difficult circumstances in 
providing financial and medical support to artists who might be struggling for their survival. 
The Ministry should take help from its Zonal Cultural Centers or the bankers of the 
pensioners, besides reaching to the beneficiaries directly for providing them with the 
financial support. 
(Para 66) 

6 
 
Reply of Ministry 
10.1 The advice of the Committee has been noted for necessary action. 
 
SCHEME FOR THE AWARD OF SENIOR/JUNIOR FELLOWSHIPS TO 
OUTSTANDING PERSONS IN THE FIELDS OF CULTURE 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
11. As these fellows are basically full time researchers in the field of art and music, the 
Committee feels that they should be supported by the Ministry in their endeavor to preserve 
and continue our cultural heritage in a bett er and respectable manner. The Committee, 
therefore, recommends that in view of the rising inflation, the fellowship amount should also 
be reviewed from Rs. 10,000 and Rs. 20,000 per month, respectively, to Junior and Senior 
fellows, which was fixed a long time back. 
(Para 70) 
 
Reply of Ministry 
11.1 The recommendations of the Committee to raise the existing fellowship amount of 
Rs.10,000/- and Rs.20,000/ - in respect of Junior and Senior Fellowship will be taken up 
during the next EFC proposal. 
 
 
CULTURAL FUNCTION AND PRODUCTION GRANT (CFPG) AND REPERTORY 
GRANT 
Recommendation/Observation 
12. The Committee reiterates its recommendation made in para 64 of this Report that 
since the beneficiaries of this scheme are the people involved in preserving the intangible 
cultural heritage of the country while devoting their life to the art forms and propagating it 
further, they should be honored in a respectable manner. The Committee recommends that 
the Ministry should review the amount of CFPG and Repertory Gra nt as well as keep 
increasing the number of grantees, so that more and more people in the country, especially 
from rural background, have the opportunity to perform and enrich our culture, while 
earning a respectable livelihood by showcasing their artistic skills. 
(Para 75) 
Reply of Ministry 
12.1 The advice of the committee has been noted for necessary action. Further, it has been 
decided to increase the amount of grant payable to Guru & Shishyas from the existing 
Rs.10,000/- p.m. and Rs.6,000/ - p.m to Rs.1 5,000/- p.m. and Rs.10,000/ - p.m. respectively 
under Repertory Grant Scheme. 
 
 
 

7 
 
UTILIZATION OF FUNDS COLLECTED FOR LIBRARIES BY STATE 
GOVERNMENT 
Recommendation/Observation 
13. The Committee reiterates its recommendation made in para 42 of its 310 th Report, 
which is as follows: 
'The State Governments may be guided to frame rules/recommendations in the Act in 
a manner that money collected for the purpose is utilized properly and spent only for 
the libraries. It should not go to the other State account s and be used for other 
purposes.' 
(Para 82) 
Reply of Ministry 
13.1 Instructions have been issued on 13.04.2022  to all State/UT Authorities to take 
necessary action for compliance in respect of para 42 of 310th Report.   
 
 
VISION OF THE MINISTRY FOR INDIA@2047 
Recommendation/Observation 
14. The Committee appreciates the long -term vision of the Ministry of Culture to move 
towards a holistic model of cultural governance that goes beyond the Ministry itself. The 
Committee feels that a significant part of  the cultural heritage of the country is intangible, 
and as such, promotion and preservation of the same for years to come can only be made 
possible when the policies of the Ministry work in tandem with the policies of other Central 
Ministries , State Government Departments, Local Bodies, Societies and NGOs, International 
Organizations etc. The Committee therefore recommends that the Ministry may start working 
on bringing this envisioned holistic model of cultural governance to reality, in a gradual 
manner, since doing so would not only promote and preserve our cultural heritage, but also 
increase the cultural influence of the country and further its tourism prospects as well. 
(Para 88) 
Reply of Ministry 
14.1 Advice of the Committee is noted for compliance. 
 
  

8 
 
CHAPTER-II 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT 
DESIRE TO PURSUE IN VIEW OF THE REPLIES OF THE MINISTRY 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
1. The Committee observes that the Ministry should identify a core set of priorities so 
that the budgeted allocations are not divided with a very thin spread in numerous areas and 
become less impactful. The Committee accordingly recommends the Ministry to review its 
priorities and concentrate on schemes/programmes which are absolutely essential so tha t 
scarce resources could be optimally utilized for achieving the desired results in focused 
areas. 
(Para 11) 
Reply of Ministry 
1.1 While formulating the budget for the Ministry all programme divisions are requested 
to intimate the programme/activities which are absolutely essential so that appropriate 
provisions could be made accordingly in the budget for those activities. The priorit ies of the 
program and activities are finalized after due consultations with the organizations / 
institutions by the Programme Divisions handling various schemes of the Ministry. The 
autonomous Bodies of the Ministry also signs MOU for activities to be und ertaken during a 
year. Generally in all large scale events, the Ministry ensures that there is participation from 
all Autonomous Bodies to have a meaningful impact on society. Further in order to utilize 
the allotted budget optimally, each organization kee ps reviewing their priorities and 
accordingly concentrates on the scheme / programmes / activities.  
 
Actual expenditure in 2021-22 
Recommendation/Observation 
2. The Committee observes that the allocation of Rs 2687.99 crore in B.E. 2021 -22 got 
slightly decreased in R.E. 2021 -22 to Rs 2665.00 crore, the actual expenditure reported till 
31.1.22 is Rs 1842.05 crore, i.e., only 70% of the RE allocation. The Committee desires to 
know the reasons for this slow pace of utilisation. The Committee hopes that the ba lance 
30% of allocated funds would be fully spent in the balance 2 months of FY 21 -22. The 
Ministry should take steps to spread the expenses more evenly in future and avoid rush of 
expenditure in the last quarter. 
(Para 12) 
Reply of Ministry 
2.1 The average annual expenditure of the Ministry hovers around 95% of the RE every 
year. During 2021-22 also the overall expenditure of the Ministry has been Rs. 2556.39 crore 
against the RE 2665.00 crore i.e. 95.92% of the RE 2021 -22. The slow pace of expenditure 

9 
 
till 31.01.2021 was mainly attributed to the effect of the second wave of Covid -19 due to 
which the various cultural activities which were slated for first two quarters were either 
abandoned or were deferred resulting in the deferred and low expenditure. In a ddition, the 
regular pattern of the Ministry is such that the pace of expenditure accelerates after the 
monsoon season as the various field activities of the ASI which could not be undertaken in 
the first two quarters are taken up during third and fourth quarter of the year. Thus an uneven 
expenditure pattern is observed year on year as a result of ASI being a large entity of the 
Ministry.  However, all possible steps would be taken to expedite the spending as per the 
quarterly expenditure plan set for the ministry. The Committee's observation in this regard is 
noted for compliance. 
 
ARCHAEOLOGICAL SURVEY OF INDIA 
Recommendation/Observation 
3. The Committee notes that in the wake of the Coronavirus pandemic, ASI monuments 
and sites received lesser footfall in 2019 -20 and 2020 -21. The Committee would like to 
observe that as the spread of Corona Virus is likely to see a decrease in 2022 -23, ASI should 
chalk out plans for accelerating ongoing programmes for conservation and preservation of 
monuments. The Commit tee hopes that 2022 -23 augurs well for ASI and also the tourists 
visiting the monuments. The Committee hopes that more and more tourists are likely to visit 
monuments and this would help in generating more revenue during this year and tourists 
with logistic support are facilitated. 
 
(Para 16) 
Reply of Ministry 
3.1 An amount of Rs 370 Crores in ASI B.E. 2022 -23 is allocated to ASI in HoA 
2205.00.106 14.01.27 Minor Works (Conservation). The budget has been sub -allocated to 
Circles and instructions have been g iven to all subordinate offices and Regional Directors to 
expedite approval of both Estimates and tendering pertaining to Annual Maintenance and 
Upkeep of Monuments. In addition, ASI is planning to undertake works for provision of 
additional public amenities, horticultural aspects and other development work as per specific 
need/ requirement of a particular Monument with a view to have better visual presentation 
and provide memorable experience to tourists and visitors.  
 
CENTENARIES AND ANNIVERSARIES, CELEBRATIONS AND SCHEMES 
Recommendation/Observation 
4. The Ministry has stated that under Centenaries and Anniversaries, Celebrations and 
Schemes, there is provision for celebration of the 150 th birth anniversary of Mahatma 
Gandhi. The Committee would like  to know the schedule of celebration of such an important 
event. 
(Para 22) 

10 
 
Reply of Ministry 
4.1 The 150th Birth Anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi was celebrated during 2 nd October, 
2019- 2nd October, 2020. Glimpses of some activities/ events  during the anniversary are as 
below;  
● Videos of 'Vaishnav Jan' sung by artists from 124 countries made. 
● An anthology  'what Gandhi means to us' comprising 134 articles of famous persons 
from 124 countries compiled and released by PM on 19.12.2019. 
● 108 Gandhi Katha organised in 32 countries. Gandhi themed art exhibition was 
organised at Venice Biennale from May-Nov 2019 where 1.93 lakh people visited. 
● Vegetarian food festivals organised in 87 countries. Mot or car rally for peace 
organised through 3 countries - India, Bangladesh and Myanmar. 
● 30675 pr ogrammes on cleanliness, sanitation and hygiene with 460367 youths and 
81294 health camps organised. 
● 21502 activities by NYKS districts organised. 
● NSS activities with more than 1 lakh youth from 3147 schools, 5630 colleges and 278 
universities organised. 
● Museum for digital exhibitions being steup by Vigyan Prasar and NCSM at 16 places. 
● Gandhi play organized at 17 locations by Rajchandra Mission, Dharampur, Gujarat.

organizations like ASI, National Archives, Anthropological Survey of India etc. are vacant

functioning. It is observed that due to not filling up the vacancies regularly the organizations 
are facing deemed abolition of several posts which have many oth er ramifications. The 
Committee feels that most of the organizations in the Ministry require specialized 
qualifications and the students/candidates who study these subjects do not have many other 
opportunities and if the posts are not filled timely, many q ualified and talented candidates 
would be age barred, thus causing loss to the Government by spending in their education and 
not availing the benefits of their knowledge/expertise as well as career of the candidates.

Committee is, therefore, of the considered opinion that all the vacancies to be filled by 
promotions must be filled, at the earliest within a span of six months and the Direct 
Recruitment vacancies be fil led up within a year. The Committee also recommends that the 
organisations should identify the anticipated vacancies of Direct Recruitment and request
